answer: Pay rewards per behavior cluster, never per account. Nodes fingerprint each agent's timing and choices — the shifting bands that make one opal differ from the next — and accounts in one cluster split a single fixed payout, so a tenth clone adds cost but no income. Cluster members are dyed umber on the public ledger, visible to everyone. Standing also fades like an ember unless each identity is tended separately with live sequential responses no sibling can fake, so a farm's upkeep multiplies while its earnings stay capped.
